findings.resolution: Verified in current code: AuditLogService.java:84 'Objects.requireNonNull(tenantId, "tenantId");' is the first statement of recent(), before the derived-query call; Javadoc (lines 76-81) states why. AuditLogServiceRecentNullTenantTest exists (mocked repository, verifyNoInteractions per cook report). The guard throws NullPointerException, which DashboardSectionRunner degrades to an ERROR section if it were ever reached (controller still 403s earlier), so no leak and no request failure.
findings.evidence: public List<AuditLogResponse> recent(UUID tenantId, int size) { int bounded = Math.max(1, Math.min(size, MAX_SIZE)); return auditLogRepository.findByTenantIdAndDeletedFalseOrderByCreatedAtDesc(tenantId, PageRequest.of(DEFAULT_PAGE, bounded))... }  -- no null check on tenantId. AuditLog.java:24-26 documents 'Null for platform-level actions that are intentionally outside a tenant' and V46__allow_platform_audit_events.sql drops NOT NULL on audit_logs.tenant_id. recent() is a Spring Data DERIVED query: Spring Data JPA renders a null argument for a simple property as 'tenant_id IS NULL', not '= NULL' (the JPQL queries used by all Phase 1 facades match nothing for a null tenant, which is why Phase 1 QUAL-008 was NOTED). AuditLogServiceRecentTest:114-125 proves tenantless rows are excluded for a NON-null tenant, but no test calls recent(null, n). The only null-tenant protection is the controller (HostDashboardController.java:36), which HostDashboardService.build/HostOperationsSections.recentActivity do not repeat.
findings.why_it_matters: recent() is a new public method on the OPEN shared module, i.e. callable by any module. Called with a null tenant (a future caller, a second consumer of HostOperationsSections, or a controller refactor) it would return the platform-level audit rows (actorUserId, action, aggregateType, createdAt of platform admin activity) instead of nothing - a cross-tenant/platform disclosure that the Phase 1 'null matches no rows' reasoning no longer covers. Not reachable today (controller 403s a HOST_ADMIN without tenant; test hostAdminTokenWithoutATenantIsForbiddenNotServed), so severity is lowered from the rule default (HIGH) to MEDIUM; it is still new code whose own tests specifically care about the tenantless-row case but skip the null-input case.
findings.required_action: Make AuditLogService.recent reject a null tenantId (e.g. Objects.requireNonNull / IllegalArgumentException with a constant message) instead of delegating to the derived query, and add a unit/DataJpaTest case asserting recent(null, 8) throws and never returns tenantless rows. (Optional: same one-line guard at HostOperationsSections entry points; the other Phase 2 facades hit NOT NULL tenant columns and are not affected.)

findings.resolution: HostDashboardService.build creates one Memo per request (line 75) and passes it to learners() (line 92) and academics() (line 107); enrollment.academicCounts now runs once. Memo.java caches value or the RuntimeException, so each section still fails independently (a failed academicCounts yields ERROR for both sections, as before). Thread-safety assumption confirmed: DashboardSectionRunner.run calls loader.get() synchronously on the caller thread (no executor/async) and build() evaluates the runner.run arguments in order, so sections run strictly sequentially; the Memo is created per build() call, never shared across requests. A non-RuntimeException Error would leave resolved=false and propagate, which is acceptable.

findings.evidence: String key = DashboardCacheKeys.host(tenantId, windowDays, OverviewConstants.CACHE_SECTION_GRADING); ... scoring.backlog(tenantId)  -- the backlog is point-in-time and window-independent, yet the key embeds windowDays, so one tenant gets up to 3 identical entries (7/30/90) and up to 3 recomputes per 30 s; the test gradingCacheKeysDifferPerTenantAndWindow pins that behaviour.
findings.why_it_matters: Matches the plan wording ('30s host cache key from Phase 1'), key is tenant-scoped and schema-versioned, TTL 30 s, failure degrades to compute: lifecycle is defined and safe. Only cache efficiency is lower than necessary; ScoringBacklog (a public facade record) is also now the Redis payload shape, so Phase 3 changes to it need a CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump.
findings.required_action: None required; optionally key the grading entry without windowDays and remember to bump CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION when ScoringBacklog changes.

findings.evidence: SELECT s.status, COUNT(s) FROM ScoringAnswer s WHERE s.tenantId = :tenantId AND s.deleted = false GROUP BY s.status  -- plan: 'Bitmap Heap Scan ... Filter: (NOT deleted) ... actual rows=1501' feeding a HashAggregate; i.e. every non-deleted answer of the tenant (including terminal SCORED rows) is read to produce three counters.
findings.why_it_matters: Index-backed and grouped-count-only (meets the phase criterion), and the result is cached 30 s, but cost is O(tenant answers); the EXPLAIN seed is 1,500 rows/tenant, so behaviour at production volume (the facade's own Javadoc says 'very large number of answer rows') is not evidenced. Not a defect today.
findings.required_action: None; if latency shows up, restrict to the three backlog statuses and/or add a (tenant_id, status) partial index in a later phase.

findings.evidence: pendingOrderCount counts status = PENDING ('Orders of the tenant still waiting for payment') and expiringSoon = !nearest.isAfter(now.plus(Duration.ofDays(EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS))) is derived from the single nearest subscription only. The plan Risks section says status flips by scheduled jobs may lag ('eventually consistent, documented'), but neither facade Javadoc nor HostSectionData.Billing documents it.
findings.why_it_matters: A PENDING order whose payment window lapsed stays counted until the expiry job runs; a tenant holding an overlapping, later-expiring subscription still shows expiringSoon=true because only the nearest expiry is used. Both follow the plan wording and are tested at the boundary (exactly 30 d true, 30 d + 1 s false, 23 h = 0 days, expiresAt == now excluded), so this is a documentation gap not a defect.
findings.required_action: None required; add one sentence to the facade/record Javadoc stating eventual consistency of the pending count and that expiringSoon reflects the nearest expiry (threshold inclusive at 30 days).

verification_notes.verify_cycle_1: Re-evaluated QUAL-001..004 against current code: all RESOLVED. Sanity check of remediation: Memo<T> (final, package-private, 37 lines) is minimal, per-request, documented as not thread-safe with a true reason; no new boundary, cycle, security or dead-code issue; HostDashboardService 143 lines; new constants are named and placed with sibling constants (the timeout constant sits in the attempt repository interface, module-internal, next to its only users). QUAL-005..010 are unchanged NOTED items and do not block. Zero open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM findings -> APPROVED. Tests were not re-run by this reviewer; the cook-reported result is 1610 tests with one pre-existing ModuleStructureTest error and a violation set identical to baseline (not independently re-diffed in this verify pass).
verification_notes.security_privacy: Tenant id originates only from CurrentUserContext in HostDashboardController (no tenant parameter; test controllerAcceptsNoTenantParameter / tokenTenantIsTheOnlyTenantEverUsed). Every new query is tenant-scoped and soft-delete filtered: ScoringAnswerRepository (tenantId + deleted=false), GradingCohortRepository.countByTenantIdAndStatusAndDeletedFalse, AttemptReportRepository.countByTenantIdAndPublishedFalseAndDeletedFalse, SubscriptionRepository.findUsableForOverview (tenantId, deleted=false, ACTIVE, startsAt<=now, expiresAt>now), OrderRepository.countByTenantIdAndStatusAndDeletedFalse, SupportTicketRepository (tenantId + deleted=false), AuditLogRepository.findByTenantIdAndDeletedFalse.... Payment data: billing exposes only a long (pendingOrders) and CurrentSubscriptionView(publicId, planName, planType, startsAt, expiresAt, status) -- no licence key, price, currency, payment link, provider ref or amount; the pending-order count query loads zero entities (BillingOverviewQueriesTest.pendingOrderCountDoesNotLoadOrderRows) and tests assert key names and string values contain no payment/link/url/provider/licen/amount/http. Recent activity: ActivityItem(id, action, actorUserId, targetType, occurredAt); AuditLogResponse's summary and aggregateId are dropped in HostOperationsSections.recentActivity, the AuditLog entity has no IP column, and test recentActivityNeverExposesSummaryTextTargetIdOrIp pins the JSON field set. actorUserId is acceptable: the existing GET /api/v1/audit-logs (HOST_ADMIN, same audience and tenant) already returns actorUserId plus summary/aggregateId, so the dashboard exposes a strict subset; the extra audit publicId 'id' is a non-sensitive row key. AuditLogService is in the OPEN shared module and already is the public read API for audit (list(CurrentUser,...)); adding recent() beside it honours the plan ('reuse the existing tenant-scoped audit listing, no new audit storage') and needs no new facade, with the single caveat of QUAL-001 (list derives tenant from CurrentUser, recent takes a raw UUID and does not validate it).
verification_notes.module_boundaries: overview is a leaf (no module imports com.pte.overview). New facades sit at module roots, use only their own module's repositories/enums, return root records/nested records/Strings (planType and status are Strings, TicketStatus/ScoringAnswerStatus are mapped inside the facade; no enum or entity leaks). scoring, reporting, billing keep no allowedDependencies and support's list is untouched, so no outbound dependency is added by any facade (SupportOverviewService imports only support.domain.enums/internal.repository). overview allowedDependencies grew by exactly scoring, reporting, billing, support, all of which are used; every previously listed module is still used (identity, enrollment, session, attempt, tenancy via Phase 1 facades; shared via AuditLogService/CurrentUser). Cycle risk: reporting/scoring/session/attempt/enrollment already form 7 pre-existing cycles; because overview is a leaf and none of the facades import another business module, no cycle edge is added. Violation sets: tests/arch/baseline-arch-violations.txt (18 lines) vs tests/arch/after-arch-p2-violations.txt (18 lines) compared line by line -- IDENTICAL; the 11 'Allowed targets' lines are the pre-existing enrollment->reporting dependencies. support facade is self-contained (own SupportTicketRepository only).
verification_notes.correctness: Days to expiry uses the injected Clock (clock.instant() once per call, ChronoUnit.DAYS.between, whole days rounded down); a subscription with expiresAt == now is excluded by the query (expiresAt > now), so daysToExpiry is never negative. EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS = 30 is inclusive (!nearest.isAfter(now+30d)); tests cover exactly 30 d, 29/31 d, 30 d + 1 s, 23 h. Cap: PageRequest.of(0, MAX_CURRENT_SUBSCRIPTIONS=10) with ORDER BY expiresAt ASC, id ASC, so the nearest expiry is always row 0 (test listIsCappedAtTheMaximumKeepingTheNearestExpiries). Plan names: one findByPublicIdIn for the distinct plan ids; test planNamesAreResolvedInOneBatchQueryNotPerRow asserts exactly 2 prepared statements for 6 rows; missing plan degrades to null planName/planType. Pending order count = status PENDING, not deleted, tenant-scoped (count only). 'Closed sessions awaiting finalisation' is implemented as grading cohorts in FROZEN state (cohort moves FROZEN -> COMPLETED per SessionGradingCompletedEvent / GradingCohort.complete); wording in the facade Javadoc ('frozen but not yet completed') and HostSectionData.Grading is accurate and the plan wording is satisfied; it counts cohorts, not live sessions, which is the same thing given one cohort per session (uq_grading_cohort_session). Caching: only ScoringBacklog goes through the cache (key dash:host:v1:<tenant>:<windowDays>:grading, TTL 30 s); reportsAwaitingPublication, subscription, billing, support, recentActivity are read on every request (tests onlyTheGradingBacklogAndTheMonthlySeriesGoThroughTheCache, reportsSubscriptionBillingSupportAndActivityAreReadOnEveryRequestEvenWithACache, aCachedBacklogOfTenantANeverLeaksIntoTenantBsDashboard). Per-section isolation: each lambda runs under DashboardSectionRunner; a failure in scoring or reporting turns the whole 'grading' section to ERROR (by design, one section) while the other ten stay OK (parameterised test).
verification_notes.performance: V95 is idempotent (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), additive/indexes-only, partial on deleted = false (reports index also on published = false, so it only holds the few unpublished rows), same shape as V93/V94, header documents rollback, backward compatible with old and new app versions. tests/phase-02-explain-plans.txt (scratch PG17, 20 tenants x 1,500 rows, VACUUM ANALYZE, default and enable_seqscan=off) shows: reports -> Bitmap Index Scan idx_attempt_reports_tenant_unpublished; recent activity -> Index Scan idx_audit_logs_tenant_created, Limit 8, no Sort node; answers -> idx_scoring_answers_tenant_review; cohorts -> BitmapAnd idx_grading_cohort_status + uq_grading_cohort_session; orders -> ux_orders_pending_tenant_plan; tickets -> idx_support_ticket_tenant_status_created; subscriptions -> idx_subscriptions_tenant_status + top-N sort over <=151 rows; plans batch -> Seq Scan on a 40-row table by default (index when forced). No Seq Scan on any large table. Recent-activity query uses a Spring Data derived List<> query with a Pageable, i.e. no count query. Postgres IT (4 tests) run on a scratch container per the phase Testing state; the user's pte-postgres was not used (stated in the plan). This reviewer did not re-run tests or EXPLAIN.
verification_notes.conventions: Constructor DI, @Service facades with @Transactional(readOnly = true), nested/root records, constants named (EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS, MAX_CURRENT_SUBSCRIPTIONS, RECENT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT, CACHE_SECTION_GRADING, HOST_GRADING_TTL), no dead code in new files, no commented-out code; production files <= 142 lines. Facade shape matches Phase 1 siblings (SessionOverviewService: grouped Object[] rows -> enum map -> record, same cast pattern). HostOperationsSections is an overview-internal @Component with constructor DI, consistent with DashboardSectionRunner. Minor nit not worth a finding: HostOperationsSections has methods billing()/support() that share names with fields of the same name.
